data.title: Suspicious invoice for a private "land registry" entry
data.summary: Grundstücksregister Online Service GmbH sent an invoice-style letter asking for €498.00 by 1 December 2026 for a two-year "entry" of the property Ackerstraße 26 in its private register. The letter itself states this is only an offer that has no connection to the official German land registry (Grundbuch).
data.explanation: This looks like an invoice but is legally only an offer (Angebot): the document itself says a contract is only formed if you pay. It describes a private, non-official listing of your property with no legal effect and no link to the real land registry (Grundbuch) kept by the local court. This matches a known scam pattern aimed at property owners. You are not obliged to pay. Before doing anything, verify the sender independently; you can also contact a consumer protection office (Verbraucherzentrale) for advice. There is no statutory deadline here since no contract exists unless you pay.

items.title: Decide whether to pay the private "land registry entry" fee
items.action: Do not pay without first verifying this is legitimate; this private registration has no official or legal value and is likely unnecessary.

warnings: This letter is a known scam/misleading-offer pattern: it mimics an official invoice but is legally only an offer, and it explicitly states the registration has no connection to the official German land registry (Grundbuch).
The entry is made in the sender's own private directory and provides no legal protection for the property; paying is not required.
Verify the company's legitimacy independently before paying anything, and consider contacting a consumer protection office (Verbraucherzentrale) or simply not responding.
